change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member raises a unique-index error (500)
findings.body: `group.add(user)` is `self.users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274), and on a saved group that inserts a GroupUser row straight away. `group_users` has a unique index on `[group_id, user_id]` (db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9). If an admin enters a username that is already in the group, or the same username twice, the insert raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and the request returns a 500. Any users earlier in the list are already added by then. The old `usernames=` path only added `expected - current`, so this didn't happen before. Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.exists?(user.id)`, and `uniq` the username list.

findings.title: remove_member leaves the user's primary_group_id pointing at the group
findings.body: The replaced `usernames=` deletion path ran `destroy_deletions` (app/models/group.rb:287-294). That destroyed each GroupUser and also ran `primary_group_id = NULL` for users whose primary group was this one. `group.users.delete(user_id)` skips both steps. A removed user keeps this group as their primary group, so its flair and title still show, and nothing tells the admin. Destroying the GroupUser row also keeps the `user_count` counter cache right (app/models/group_user.rb:2). Use `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all` and clear `primary_group_id` the same way `destroy_deletions` does.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` returns 2 for 50 members with limit 50, and 3 for 100. The pager shows an extra page, and `next` moves offset to `user_count` (line 33), which loads an empty member list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently shows only the first 50 members
findings.body: Before this change, `/groups/:name/members` returned every member of non-automatic groups. Now it defaults to `limit 50` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22), and the public route calls `model.findMembers()` with the model's default limit of 50 (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10). This template has no pager, so any group with more than 50 members shows a truncated list with no sign that more exist. Add next/previous controls here, as in the admin template, or keep loading everything on this page.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember have no failure handling, and the input is not cleared
findings.body: When `/admin/groups/:id/members` rejects (for example a 422 on an automatic group, or the 500 above), the promise rejects with no handler, so the admin sees nothing. On success the usernames stay in the selector (the TODO on line 62 says so). Add a rejection handler that shows the error, and reset `usernames` on success.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit
findings.body: Anyone who can see the group can pass `limit=1000000` and get every member serialized in one request. Before, only automatic groups were paginated, and the default there was 200. Cap the limit, e.g. `[limit, 200].min`.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses PUT while the route is DELETE
findings.body: The route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (config/routes.rb:49), but this spec sends `xhr :put`. It still passes because controller specs dispatch by action name and don't check the HTTP verb. Use `xhr :delete` so the spec matches the real request. No spec covers adding a user who is already a member, or `primary_group_id` after a removal.

contracts.before_after: The old path computed additions as expected - current before building GroupUsers. The new path pushes every user found, with no membership check.
contracts.visible_effect: On success the client reloads members through findMembers; the user list and count update.
contracts.failure_mode: A duplicate member hits the unique index and returns a 500. The client has no rejection handler, so the failure is silent.

contracts.action: Admin removes a member via DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members
contracts.before_after: The old path destroyed each GroupUser and nulled primary_group_id. The new path deletes the join row without either step.
contracts.visible_effect: The member disappears from the list, but their primary group flair stays.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejection is unhandled, so the failure is silent.

contracts.action: Members fetch now paginated and stored on the Group model
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous afterModel loading in both routes
contracts.before_after: Before, routes waited for the members in afterModel. Now setupController fires the fetch without waiting, and the result sets `members` on the model.
contracts.visible_effect: The list renders once the fetch resolves. The public page is capped at 50 with no pager.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected fetch is unhandled and leaves the list empty, with no error shown.

summary: The PR replaces the bulk usernames field with paginated listing and add/remove-member endpoints. There are four fix-level problems. Adding a user who is already a member hits the group_users unique index and returns a 500. remove_member skips the primary_group_id cleanup the old path did. totalPages is off by one when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. The public members page now quietly shows only the first 50 members because it has no pager. Smaller points: the add/remove calls have no error handling, the public members endpoint accepts any limit, and one spec uses PUT where the route is DELETE.
